source_refs.note: Exercise 5.1 (book p. 154), Question 3; answer key PDF 306 (Answers 5.1, key numbered 4).

blocks.prompt: 3. The vertices of \(\triangle PQR\) are \(P(1, 2)\), \(Q(5, -6)\) and \(R(7, -2)\). Find the equations of all three medians.
blocks.explanation:
Median woh line hai jo kisi vertex ko samne wali side ke mid-point se milati hai. Triangle ke teen vertices hain, is liye teen medians.
Har median ke do points maloom ho jayenge: vertex aur mid-point. Jab do points hon to two-point form sab se seedha hai (kitab ne Example 7 mein yahi kiya).
Plan: pehle teeno mid-points, phir teen two-point equations.
Ek median mein dono points ka \(y\) barabar aayega; wahan seedha horizontal line likhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(P(1, 2)\), \(Q(5, -6)\), \(R(7, -2)\).
Maloom karna: medians \(PD\), \(QE\), \(RF\), jahan \(D\), \(E\), \(F\) sides \(QR\), \(PR\), \(PQ\) ke mid-points hain.
Tareeqa: mid-point formula aur two-point form \(\frac{y - y_1}{y_2 - y_1} = \frac{x - x_1}{x_2 - x_1}\).
Ek chhoti si tip: median ka naam hamesha vertex aur mid-point ke harf se rakhein (\(PD\), \(QE\), \(RF\)), is se ghalat side lene ka khatra kam ho jata hai.

Mid-points
\[D\left(\dfrac{5 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{-6 - 2}{2}\right) = D(6, -4)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 - 2}{2}\right) = E(4, 0)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{1 + 5}{2}, \dfrac{2 - 6}{2}\right) = F(3, -2)\]
Kyun: har median apne vertex ke samne wali side ke mid-point par khatam hota hai. \(P\) ke samne \(QR\), \(Q\) ke samne \(PR\), \(R\) ke samne \(PQ\).
Dhyan dein: ghalat side ka mid-point le lena aam ghalti hai; pehle tay karein kaunsi side kis vertex ke samne hai.

Median \(QE\)
\[\dfrac{y + 6}{0 + 6} = \dfrac{x - 5}{4 - 5}\]
\[-(y + 6) = 6(x - 5)\]
\[6x + y - 24 = 0\]
Kyun: \(Q(5, -6)\) aur \(E(4, 0)\) se two-point form. \(y - (-6) = y + 6\); minus ka minus plus.

Median \(RF\)
\(R(7, -2)\) aur \(F(3, -2)\) dono ka \(y\)-coordinate \(-2\) hai, is liye line horizontal hai:
\[y = -2\]
\[y + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: two-point form mein denominator \(y_2 - y_1 = 0\) aa jata, aur zero se divide nahi ho sakta. Jab dono points ka \(y\) ek ho to line seedhi \(y = \) wahi number hoti hai.

Tasdeeq:
Teeno medians centroid \(\left(\frac{1 + 5 + 7}{3}, \frac{2 - 6 - 2}{3}\right) = \left(\frac{13}{3}, -2\right)\) se guzarne chahiyein:
\[6\left(\tfrac{13}{3}\right) + 5(-2) - 16 = 0\]
\[6\left(\tfrac{13}{3}\right) + (-2) - 24 = 0\]
aur \(y = -2\) bhi poori hai. Teeno ek point par milte hain, aur jawab answer key (number 4) se milta hai.
